contains: 210-acre woodland botanical garden
4.5 miles of shoreline

facts.text: Garvan Woodland Gardens is a 210-acre woodland botanical garden on a forested peninsula in Lake Hamilton, with about 4.5 miles of shoreline.

contains: owned by the University of Arkansas
Fay Jones School of Architecture and Design

facts.text: The garden is owned by the University of Arkansas and run through its Fay Jones School of Architecture and Design.
facts.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: About 44 acres are the developed tour area

facts.text: About 44 acres are the developed tour area; the rest of the peninsula is pine, oak and hickory woodland.
facts.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: began the garden in 1956
laid out the paths and chose the plants herself

facts.text: Verna Cook Garvan began the garden in 1956. Self-taught, she laid out the paths and chose the plants herself over about 40 years.
facts.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: Arthur B. Cook of Malvern bought it for timber
made the land a peninsula

facts.text: In the 1920s Arthur B. Cook of Malvern bought the land for timber. Carpenter Dam then created Lake Hamilton, which made it a peninsula.
facts.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: In 1985 she signed a trust agreement
She died in 1993

facts.text: In 1985 Verna Garvan signed a trust agreement giving the property to the University of Arkansas landscape architecture program. She died in 1993.
facts.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: renamed Garvan Woodland Gardens
dedicated on April 7, 2002

facts.text: Building the public garden began in March 2000, when it was renamed Garvan Woodland Gardens. It was dedicated on April 7, 2002.

contains: More than 125,000 visitors come each year

facts.text: More than 125,000 visitors come to the garden each year.
facts.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: Opened in September 2006, designed by Maurice Jennings and David McKee
57-foot ceiling

facts.text: Anthony Chapel opened in September 2006. Designed by Maurice Jennings and David McKee, it is wood, glass and steel with yellow-pine beams and a 57-foot ceiling.

contains: Anthony Family Carillon is a bell tower of 16 copper-clad

facts.text: The Anthony Family Carillon beside the chapel is a bell tower of 16 copper-clad columns.

contains: By E. Fay Jones and Maurice Jennings
oculus shaped like an unfolding flower

facts.text: The Verna C. Garvan Pavilion, by E. Fay Jones and Maurice Jennings, is open-air sandstone and redwood under a glass roof with an oculus shaped like an unfolding flower.
facts.source: Garvan Woodland Gardens: Garvan Pavilion and Terrace

contains: about 4 acres in a natural ravine
12-foot waterfall and a half-acre koi pond

facts.text: The Garden of the Pine Wind is a Japanese garden of about 4 acres in a natural ravine, with cascades, pools, a 12-foot waterfall and a half-acre koi pond.

contains: Bridge of the Full Moon (stone, 11 feet high, with a circular

facts.text: The Joy Manning Scott Bridge of the Full Moon is a stone bridge 11 feet high with a circular opening.

contains: named by the mayor of Hanamaki, Japan, Hot Springs' sister city

facts.text: The Sunrise Bridge was named by the mayor of Hanamaki, Japan, Hot Springs' sister city.

contains: white azaleas are clipped to look like clouds

facts.text: At the Floating Cloud Bridge, white azaleas are clipped to look like clouds.

contains: nearly three dozen bonsai and penjing

facts.text: The Weyerhaeuser Bonsai Garden by the entrance shows nearly three dozen bonsai and penjing.

contains: 120-foot winding walkway on stone piers about two stories up

facts.text: The Millsap Canopy Bridge is a 120-foot winding walkway on stone piers about two stories up, over Singing Springs Gorge.

contains: cave behind a 12-foot waterfall
450-foot elevated walkway

facts.text: The Evans Children's Adventure Garden has a cave behind a 12-foot waterfall, a rock maze, wading pools and a 450-foot elevated walkway.

contains: By Modus Studio of Fayetteville

facts.text: The Bob and Sunny Evans Tree House, by Modus Studio of Fayetteville in steel and heat-treated pine, opened June 30, 2018.

contains: 45 acres of dense forest on the north side
Birdsong Trail

facts.text: The Hixson Family Nature Preserve is 45 acres of dense forest on the north side, with the Birdsong Trail and bird feeding stations.

contains: The westernmost point: a flagstone terrace over Lake Hamilton

facts.text: The Perry Wildflower Overlook is the westernmost point: a flagstone terrace over Lake Hamilton beside a wildflower meadow.
facts.source: Garvan Woodland Gardens: Perry Wildflower Overlook

contains: G-scale trains on 389 feet of track
Malvern Brick & Tile

facts.text: The Sugg Model Train Garden runs G-scale trains on 389 feet of track, past miniatures of Malvern Brick & Tile and the Cook family's lumber mill.

contains: flagstone seating for 500

facts.text: The Klipsch Amphitheater sits in a natural hollow in the middle of the gardens, with flagstone seating for 500 under tall pines.

contains: Wood and native stone, designed by French Harris of Hot Springs

facts.text: The Pratt Welcome Center, in wood and native stone, was designed by French Harris of Hot Springs. It holds the gate, the GardenShop and the Magnolia Room.
facts.source: Encyclopedia of Arkansas: Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: More than 160 varieties of azaleas

facts.text: The garden grows more than 160 varieties of azaleas.

contains: about 100 plants of 50 cultivars along a quarter-mile camellia trail

facts.text: About 100 camellias of 50 cultivars line a quarter-mile camellia trail; Garvan is on the American Camellia Trail.
facts.source: American Camellia Society: Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: George can be
usually near the Pratt Welcome Center

facts.text: A peacock named George roams the grounds, usually near the Pratt Welcome Center.
facts.source: Arkansas Tourism: Birding at Garvan Woodland Gardens

contains: Dogs are welcome on a leash of 6 feet or less

facts.text: Dogs are welcome on a leash of 6 feet or less, but not in the chapel, the treehouse, the ponds or during Holiday Lights.

contains: About 150,000 tulips of about 150 varieties
hand-planted in designed shapes marked out with string

facts.text: The Tulip Extravaganza shows about 150,000 tulips of about 150 varieties, hand-planted in designed shapes marked out with string lines.

contains: treated as annuals and replanted every year
USDA Zone 8

facts.text: The tulips are treated as annuals and replanted every year: Hot Springs is now USDA Zone 8, too warm for most tulips to come back.

contains: moved planting later, into January
150,000 tulips in 10 days

facts.text: Staff moved tulip planting later, into January, so tulips would not bloom while the garden is closed. For the 2026 show the crew planted 150,000 tulips in 10 days.

contains: sustained hard freeze in the mid-20s

facts.text: Brief dips below freezing are fine for tulips, but a sustained hard freeze in the mid-20s °F damages the blooms.

contains: closed for all of January and reopens about February 1

facts.text: The garden closes for all of January and reopens about February 1.

contains: tens of thousands of daffodils bloom first

facts.text: Daffodil Days open the season: crocus, hyacinths and tens of thousands of daffodils bloom first after the garden reopens.

contains: Japanese maples, chrysanthemums and fall annuals
more than 8,000 mums

facts.text: Fall in the Woodlands brings Japanese maples, chrysanthemums and fall annuals; past displays used more than 8,000 mums.

contains: Lake Hamilton shoreline, road and ditch cleanup

facts.text: Trash Bash is an annual Lake Hamilton shoreline, road and ditch cleanup each fall.

contains: November 21 to December 31
about 5 to 9:30 PM

facts.text: Holiday Lights runs at night, about 5 to 9:30 PM; in 2026 from November 21 to December 31.

contains: roughly 50-foot tree with a 12 to 15 minute musical light show

facts.text: The Rose Tree is a roughly 50-foot tree with a 12 to 15 minute musical light show.

contains: installation begins around September 15
about 150 pole trees, about 60 wrapped trees

facts.text: A 2026 university contract has Holiday Lights installation begin around September 15, with about 150 pole trees, 60 wrapped trees and 300 set pieces over about 20 acres.

contains: about 46 weeks of work a year
Volunteers cannot operate machinery

facts.text: Holiday Lights takes about 46 weeks of work a year. Some elements weigh over 300 pounds, and volunteers cannot operate machinery.

contains: about 200 weddings a year

facts.text: The garden hosts about 200 weddings a year.

contains: In 2012 the garden closed for the rest of the year after a winter storm

facts.text: In 2012 the garden closed for the rest of the year after a winter storm and power outages.
